title: Nine ways to love God
hookLine: nine ways to love God, and a well-known name standing beside each one
carry: navadha bhakti: nine ways to love God
tomorrow: a girl wears God's garland before he does
last: A LEAF, A FLOWER, A FRUIT, WATER.

lines: SAY IT, SHOW IT, SHOW UP.
cards: People love differently. Some say it. Some show it with food.
Some just show up, every time, and never say a word. Some love by listening, really listening. In plenty of families the love is all there; it just comes in different shapes.

Prahlada's list is the bhakti tradition noticing the same thing about loving God. It's not one feeling. It's nine doors into the same room, and tradition even gives each door a well-known person who walked through it.

teach.h: THE EAR, THE VOICE, THE MIND.
teach.b: Here they are, in the order Prahlada gives them in the Bhagavata Purana. One: shravana, hearing the stories of God. Tradition's example is King Parikshit, who heard the whole Bhagavata before he died.
Two: kirtana, singing praise aloud: the sage Shuka, who told Parikshit those stories. Three: smarana, remembering, keeping God in mind: Prahlada himself.
Four: pada-sevana, serving the feet, humble, close service: the goddess Lakshmi, at Vishnu's feet. Five: archana, worship with offerings, lamp and flower and water: King Prithu.

teach.h: THE HANDS AND THE BOWED HEAD.
teach.b: Six: vandana, bowing and praising: Akrura, who bowed to the ground when he met Krishna. Seven: dasya, being a servant: Hanuman, who wanted nothing but to serve Rama.

Eight: sakhya, friendship: Arjuna, whose chariot Krishna drove into battle, as a friend. Nine: atma-nivedana, giving your whole self: King Bali, who gave everything he had, even his own head to be stepped on.
Notice how the list moves: the ear, then the voice, then the mind. Then the hands, then the whole body bowing.
And it ends with a person handing over themselves. It's a ladder, and it's also a menu. Some teachers say a person may find one or two doors that fit and live there for years.
A grandmother who can't sit through a sermon but sings every evening. A quiet man who never sings but sweeps the temple steps. Same room.
That's the teaching, navadha bhakti: there isn't one right feeling for loving God.
There are nine ways in, and the tradition honors every one.

how: Hindu devotional teachers often present the nine forms of bhakti from the Bhagavata Purana as a range of practices, from listening to sacred stories and singing to service and complete self-offering, and devotees tend to settle into the forms that suit them.

o: loving God by hearing, singing, serving and more
nine fixed rituals that must be done in order
a single feeling only saints can ever reach

games.q: the door and who walked through it — tap the pairs.

s: the nine forms of devotion must be practiced in strict order
it's a ladder and also a menu: some teachers say a person may live in one or two doors for years.
the list of nine comes from Prahlada in the Bhagavata Purana
he gives it in answer to his father's question about the best thing he'd learned.
friendship with God is one of the nine forms
sakhya, friendship: tradition's example is Arjuna, whose chariot Krishna drove as his friend.

games.q: a grandmother can't follow a long sermon, but sings to Krishna every evening. by the nine forms, is she practicing bhakti?
o: no: she has to learn the philosophy first.
yes: kirtana, singing, is one of the nine doors.
only if she also does all eight others.
games.why: singing, kirtana, is the second of the nine. each door opens into the same room.

practice: Walk slowly past the nine doors: hearing, singing, remembering, serving at the feet, offering, bowing, being a servant, friendship, giving yourself. Notice which one feels like home, not the one you think is best, and stay with it.
If you pray, walk through that door now, quietly; if you don't, just notice which shape your love usually takes, with anyone.

wordCard.voice: Bhakti yoga. The nine forms of devotion, navadha bhakti: hearing, singing, remembering, serving, worship, bowing, servanthood, friendship and giving yourself.

orig.note: Sanskrit: navadhā bhakti, devotion in nine forms (nava, nine), as listed in the Bhagavata Purana 7.5.23–24.

carryVoice: Your line: navadha bhakti, nine ways to love God. Nine doors open into one room. Until tomorrow, then.
